A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TokenTiming and contain 19 readable pages. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-pair benchmarks, task-level speedups, DTW ablations and runtime analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original experiments and adds specialized-model and multilingual results in Appendices M and O.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the decoding, candidate-length and preprocessing procedures are unchanged. Appendix A explains terminal-token and copied-probability mapping rules already illustrated in v1 Figure 1; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix O newly documents Arabic evaluation alongside previously mentioned languages; v1 listed nine other validation languages. The main Spec-Bench tasks remain unchanged. Appendix M introduces specialized backbones but does not identify new medical or coding datasets.

E2.justification: AR and TLI remain the main comparators, and Figure 4 retains Medusa and EAGLE-1/2/3. The new specialized-model comparison also uses TLI. Additional draft–target configurations do not introduce new comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols pair Qwen2.5-0.5B with BioMistral-7B and Qwen2.5-Coder-14B, and hold a Llama-3.1-70B/Qwen2.5-0.5B pair fixed across languages of the same corpus. Table 1 adds maximum-vocabulary-normalized overlap. Existing generation hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix O adds language-specific speedup and DTW-offset analysis, including Figure 13, to examine alignment behavior across tokenization conditions. Existing window-size, repetition, candidate-length and CPU/GPU analyses remain. Appendix N explains existing tuning rather than adding an ablation.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains the same overhead uncertainty, 0.003 ± 0.002. V3 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands reported findings through five additional model-pair result sets in Tables 1–2, specialized-model results in Table 8, and quantified language results and offsets in Table 11/Figure 13. BioMistral-7B achieves 1.31x with TokenTiming versus 1.15x with TLI; multilingual speedups include French at 2.23x and Chinese at 1.06x. Existing main-table performance values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a string-consistency lemma and probability-mapping consistency arguments for many-to-one and one-to-many alignments, invoking tokenizer invertibility and draft–target approximation. These substantially extend v1's generic acceptance/rejection proof, which remains in shortened form.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the core claims of universal, retraining-free, lossless speculative decoding and the headline 1.57x and 2.27x speedups. Added evidence does not redefine the claimed contributions.

C2.justification: V1's tentative morphology/vocabulary-overlap explanation and language-coverage caveat give way to Appendix O's stronger character-level versus word/subword tokenization account. Section 5.2.7 also newly asserts that the remaining 85% of samples represent typical generation.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly documents probability-mapping cases, selection of global w = 8 using offset CDFs and mean speedup, and approximately 15% exclusion for repetitive outputs. These clarify existing implementation and filtering practices. Hardware, generation hyperparameters and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kudo and Richardson's SentencePiece reference and Xu et al.'s repetition study to support its language and filtering discussions. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against existing speculative-decoding methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in Appendix A, the repetition-filtering paragraph and the replacement of the standalone limitations discussion with Appendix O. Appendices M–O and revised affiliations are added, but most main-text wording and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain rows, Table 1 gains overlap columns, and v3 adds Tables 8 and 11 and Figure 13. Figure 1 is lightly restyled and several appendix displays move. Existing experimental plots and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Additional results and implementation disclosures improve completeness and transparency. However, the new Appendix A consistency arguments do not establish that terminal/copied probabilities equal the actual proposal probabilities required by the losslessness derivation. The expanded Table 1 also leaves the DeepSeek TLI peak misstated in prose: 1.09x versus the newly reported 1.21x. Benefits coexist with weaknesses in the central mathematical justification and reporting, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
